title: Rolling KV reconciliation with snapshot hedging and traffic microwindows
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Private (VPC) runtime upgrades that touch KV cache layout or eviction semantics currently risk observable request latency spikes and session-level inconsistency during cutover. This ticket scopes a zero-downtime rollout pattern that combines snapshot hedging (pre-warm snapshots taken from live primed nodes), rolling KV reconciliation (pairwise reconcile between old/new runtime nodes), and short traffic microwindows (controlled, short-duration incremental traffic shifts) orchestrated by Terraform hooks and the upgrade operator. Goals: 1) Ensure no user session sees a stale or missing KV state during switchover. 2) Limit tail-latency regressions to <5% relative to baseline. 3) Provide deterministic, automated rollback within 2 minutes of failure detection. Non-goals: large schema or epoch-changing KV migrations (those will be separate migration jobs). Acceptance criteria: - Automated orchestration that runs in staging and 2 customer VPCs successfully. - Canary pass signals (latency, error-rate, KV-hit-rate) implemented and wired to the operator. - Rollback runs automatically when health gate fails and leaves the cluster in a consistent state with no 500-class errors. Design summary: - Terraform/IaC: add a new module `modules/upgrade_hooks` exposing plan-time checks and apply-time lifecycle null_resource hooks that call the operator API to start a staged rollout. The module will surface variables for microwindow size, reconciliation batch size, and synthetic probe config. - Operator behavior: 1) prewarm phase: snapshot hedging copies current KV prefixes into a primed snapshot store accessible by new nodes (S3 or customer-backed blob). 2) pairwise reconcile phase: for each tenant slice, create a temporary shims that mirror requests to both old and new runtime and reconcile KV deltas using deterministic merge rules. 3) traffic microwindows: increment traffic in small fixed-duration windows (e.g., 30s windows, 2% increments) while monitoring health gates. 4) commit or rollback: on success, cut traffic to new nodes; on failure, revert traffic and roll back Terraform plan. Observability and health gates: - Metrics: per-slice request latency (p50/p95/p99), kv_hit_ratio, kv_reconcile_conflicts, synthetic_probe_success_rate, error_rate_5xx. - Health gate logic: sliding window evaluation that requires p95 < baseline*1.15 and kv_reconcile_conflicts == 0 and probe_success_rate >= 99% for 3 consecutive windows. - Telemetry: trace metadata to link requests that observed dual-path reconciliation to aid debugging. Rollback plan: - Fast path: operator initiates traffic reversal and marks new node set as drainable; Terraform revert hook runs to reapply previous instance group identity. - Consistency path: if reconcile conflicts > threshold, run a forced merge job that replays snapshot hedged data into the older nodes before switching back. - Postmortem obligations: automatic incident ticket with golden telemetry snapshot and list of affected tenants. Terraform/IaC considerations: - Use null_resource local-exec hooks sparingly; prefer invoking an operator controller by patching a CRD-like record written to the control plane (control plane in customer VPC). - Add a preflight `terraform plan` validator that ensures no overlapping instance-group renames within the same rolling window. - Store hedged snapshots in encrypted blobstore with KMS key referenced by deployment variables. Safety testing and validation: - Run chaos experiments in staging: pod-kill ramp during microwindows, network partition on primed snapshot retrieval, and synthetic KV divergence injection. - Test with synthetic traffic harness (Drive/bench) and Shadow traffic to validate microwindow thresholds. - Run a canary on two low-impact customer VPCs before general rollout. Implementation notes: - Build a lightweight reconcile-agent binary that can run as an init-container to perform local KV reconciliation before full admission. - Implement reconciliation idempotency via vector-clock style metadata stored alongside keys. - Expose CLI and API endpoints for manual interventions: pause, force-commit, force-rollback, snapshot-inspect. Related artifacts: design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/kv-reconcile-hedging, terraform module proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3291, operator proof-of-concept PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/112.
